issues.where: signals(), acceptance loop, lines 392-412: the exit flag is written (`if j + hold < nd: xi = int(e_idx[j + hold]); if xi - 1 > ei: ... s.exit_long[xi - 1] = True` / `s.exit_short[xi - 1] = True`) BEFORE the stop-touch scan, and it is never removed when the scan then finds `flat_at = ei + 1 + int(hit[0]) < xi`
issues.issue: Rule mismatch in the hold_days = 3 arm: a leftover exit flag closes a different trade. If trade A (signal at E(D)) is stopped out at bar h before X_A - 1, the module sets flat_at = h and correctly accepts a later shock signal B at E(D+1) or E(D+2) (shock days cluster, so this is common). A's flag at X_A - 1 = E(D+3) - 1 is still in the array, and the executor reads `exit_long[i - 1]` / `exit_short[i - 1]` for whatever position is open, so a same-side trade B is closed at the open of E(D+3) after 1-2 days instead of its own 3. Measured on design years 2010-2017 with the executor (0.2 pip slippage), counting trades whose REASON_SIGNAL exit bar differs from their own X: hold 3, k 1.0, v 0.0 -> EURUSD 23/222, GBPUSD 17/223, AUDUSD 11/222, USDJPY 18/206, AUDJPY 17/197, XAUUSD 15/224; v 1.3 -> 4/43, 1/33, 4/47, 5/57, 3/44, 3/54; k 1.25 and v 1.5 cells also affected (up to 4/44 USDJPY, 2/12 AUDJPY). The hold_days = 1 arm is clean (0 in every cell): A's flag sits at E(D+1) - 1, before any later signal bar, so it can never meet another trade. The same leftover can in principle arise when the max_bars cap binds before X (end < xi but the flag at xi - 1 was already written); that case is rare but has the same fix.
issues.fix: Run the stop scan first and write the exit flag only if the trade is still open at X - 1. Concretely, replace lines 392-412 with: `end = m.n; xi = -1` / `if j + hold < nd: xi = int(e_idx[j + hold]); if xi - 1 > ei: end = xi` / `end = min(end, ei + 1 + max_bars, m.n); flat_at = end` / (unchanged stop scan that may set flat_at = ei + 1 + hit[0]) / `if xi > 0 and end == xi and flat_at == xi: s.exit_long[xi - 1] = True if is_long else s.exit_short[xi - 1] = True` (written as an if/else). This is causal: the flag at bar xi - 1 then depends only on bid_l/ask_h of bars ei+1..xi-1, all at or before the flag bar. I applied exactly this patch to a scratch copy and re-ran the count: 0 foreign-flag closes in all 36 hold-3 cells (6 markets x k x v), signals == trades still holds everywhere, and the hold-1 arm is unchanged.

issues.where: stop simulation, lines 405-410: `stop = m.ask_o[ei + 1] - dist` / `stop = m.bid_o[ei + 1] + dist`
issues.issue: The executor sets the stop from the slipped fill (long: ask_o + slippage - sl_dist; short: bid_o - slippage + sl_dist), so the module's stop sits slippage further away. The module therefore finds a stop touch at the same bar as the executor or later, never earlier, so its flat_at is never earlier than the real flat bar. That is the safe direction: no signal is written that the executor would ignore (confirmed: signals == trades in every cell), and no extra stray flag can follow. The cost is that when a bar's low lands inside the 0.2-pip band, a later shock signal between the real stop and the module's flat_at is dropped. This is a small, conservative loss of trades, not a leak.
issues.fix: No change needed. Optionally widen the touch test by a small tolerance (for example m.pip * 0.2 for FX) so the band is closed; do not narrow it, because narrowing would let the module think the trade is flat before the executor does.

issues.where: E(D) = last bar with close <= 20:00 (line 340, `hi = np.searchsorted(close_t, t_end, side='right'); e_idx = hi - 1`) and the exit flag at X - 1
issues.issue: Knowing that bar i is the last bar closing at or before 20:00, or the bar just before E(D+hold), uses the timestamp of the next bar, not its prices. For the entry this is harmless: the fill is the first bar after E, which is exactly what a live trader acting at 20:00 UTC gets, and all price inputs are at or before E. For the exit, it differs from live only when the 19:00 H1 bar is missing (an H1 hour with no ticks on a weekday afternoon, which is very rare on these six markets). The truncation and perturbation probes pass.
issues.fix: None required; it matches the rules as written and the oracle pattern (flag on xi - 1). Note it in the stage C report if any XAUUSD or holiday dates show missing 19:00 bars.

lookahead_risk: Low for prices. Every feature at signal bar E(D) uses closed bars only: C(D) = bid_c[E(D)] and C(D_prev) from earlier bars; V(D) = cum_vol[hi_D] - cum_vol[hi_Dprev] covers bars closing in (20:00 D_prev, 20:00 D], all at or before E(D); Vbar counts only valid V strictly before D (searchsorted side='left' on valid positions, so the current V is excluded); ATR is F.atr_prev mapped through daily.to_bars to E(D), known at the start of that trading day. The acceptance logic is causal: to decide whether a later signal at bar ei' is skipped, the comparison ei' < flat_at only depends on whether the earlier trade's stop was touched in bars <= ei' (if it was, flat_at <= ei'; if not, flat_at > ei' whatever later bars do), on the earlier exit and cap bars (deterministic indices), and recursively on earlier accepted signals. The proposed exit-flag fix keeps this: the flag at xi - 1 depends only on bars ei+1..xi-1. Executor semantics were checked line by line: the stop is checked on the fill bar (the module scan starts at ei+1, the fill bar); the exit flag on bar i-1 is applied at the open of i, before any inside-bar stop; the time exit fires when i - e_i >= max_bars, i.e. at the open of ei+1+max_bars, which matches the module's cap; and a signal on the bar where the position closes is registered (side == 0 after the manage block), which matches the module's 'ei >= flat_at accepted'. The automated truncation, perturbation and determinism probes pass. The only residual is the timestamp-only look-ahead noted in the third issue, which is benign.
notes: Everything else matches the pre-registered rules and the Director's ruling. (1) v = 0.0 is a true control: climax = isfinite(vol) & isfinite(vbar) & (vbar > 0) & (vol >= v * vbar) is the only volume test, and there is no extra V >= Vbar floor. The control arm keeps the same Vbar-valid start as the other arms, as the rules require ('Require Vbar(D) > 0 and V(D) finite'). (2) E(D) window (16:00, 20:00] on close times = ts + 1h; Monday to Friday only; D_prev gap <= 4 calendar days; Monday windows include Friday evening and Sunday, as specified; XAUUSD artefact volume is not filtered. (3) The side fades ret; sl_dist = sl_atr * ATR20_prev, skipped when NaN or <= 0 (shock requires atr > 0 and is finite); tp NaN by default; entry_type 0 and valid_bars 1 by default; max_bars = 24 * (hold + 3). (4) Parameter plumbing: k, v and hold_days are read from p and present in PARAMS; sl_atr is in PARAMS (fixed at 1.0, not gridded, as registered); the extra keys ref_start_utc, ref_end_utc, max_gap_days and vol_window carry the registered constants. (5) The one blocker is the leftover exit flag of a stopped-out trade closing the next same-side trade in the hold_days = 3 arm (5-11% of hold-3 trades in the v = 0 cells, also present in filtered cells). It would bias hold 3 against the 1-day comparison and corrupt the hold-dimension surface. The two-line fix is given above and has been verified on a scratch copy (0 foreign closes in 36 cells).
